element.name: Patch & Software Maintenance

element.name: Data Protection & Cryptography
element.documentation: Protect data at rest and in transit, and manage keys and cardholder data scope.

element.name: Data-at-Rest Protection
element.documentation: Protect stored data with encryption and key management to policy.

element.name: Data-in-Transit Protection

element.name: Privacy Management

element.name: Contact Handling & Routing

element.name: Contact Center Operations

element.name: Contact Routing

element.name: Account Maintenance & Servicing Requests

element.name: Digital Self-Service

element.name: Correspondence & Notification Management

element.name: Complaint Capture & Resolution

element.name: Hardship & Payment Assistance

element.name: Market & Competitive Analysis

element.name: Portfolio Strategy & Investment Planning

element.name: Enterprise Architecture & Change Portfolio

element.name: Merger, Acquisition & Portfolio Transaction

element.name: Software Development & Management

element.name: Secure Development

element.name: Platform & Infrastructure Operations

element.name: Infrastructure & Platform Management
element.documentation: Provision and operate compute, storage, network, and platform services.

element.name: Capacity & Performance Management

element.name: Service Management & Incident Response
element.documentation: Detect, triage, and resolve service incidents.

element.name: Service Desk
element.documentation: Single point of contact for users: intake, triage, and communication.

element.name: Incident Management

element.name: Problem Management

element.name: Release & Change Management

element.name: Release Management

element.name: Deployment Management

element.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery

element.name: Enterprise Integration & API Management

element.name: End-User Computing & Workplace Technology
element.documentation: Equip and support the workforce with workplace technology.

element.name: IT Asset Management
element.documentation: Track hardware and software assets through their lifecycle and cost.

element.name: Service Request Management
element.documentation: Fulfill standard requests through defined, often automated, paths.

element.name: Quality Engineering & Testing
element.documentation: Prove that a change does what it claims before and after it reaches production: test strategy, automation, performance, acceptance, defects, and release certification.

element.name: Third-Party & Vendor Management
element.documentation: Third-Party & Vendor Management. Level 0 enterprise capability domain (Enable tier).

element.name: Vendor Sourcing & Due Diligence
element.documentation: Select and diligence suppliers.

element.name: Contract & SLA Management
element.documentation: Contract suppliers and hold them to commitments.

element.name: Ongoing Vendor Risk Monitoring
element.documentation: Monitor supplier risk through the life of the relationship.

element.name: Ongoing Third-Party Monitoring
element.documentation: Monitor supplier risk posture continuously between assessments.

element.name: Third-Party Performance Review
element.documentation: Review supplier performance and risk on the contracted cadence.

element.name: Vendor Exit & Continuity Planning
element.documentation: Maintain exit and continuity plans for critical suppliers.

element.name: Third-Party Servicing Delivery
element.documentation: Third-Party Servicing Delivery. Level 0 enterprise capability domain (Core tier).

element.name: Client Program Configuration & Setup
element.documentation: Configure platform, product, and treatment for a client program.

element.name: Portfolio Conversion & Deconversion
element.documentation: Convert client portfolios onto and off the servicing platform.

element.name: Client Reporting & Data Exchange
element.documentation: Deliver contracted reporting and data feeds to clients.

element.name: Client Billing & Revenue Management
element.documentation: Bill servicing fees and manage revenue recognition.

element.name: Client Audit & Oversight Support
element.documentation: Support client and client-regulator oversight activity.

element.name: Client-Directed Change Management
element.documentation: Intake, price, and deliver client-requested change.

element.name: Refine and prioritize the product backlog
element.documentation: Break approved demand into sized, ordered work items with acceptance criteria, and agree the next increment with the business owner.

element.name: Design and build a software increment
element.documentation: Design, implement, and unit-test a work item to its acceptance criteria within the agreed architecture and standards.

element.name: Review and merge code
element.documentation: Peer-review a change for correctness, security, and standards before it is merged to the main line. Merge rights sit with reviewers, not authors, which is the segregation the change-control audit tests; review evidence stays on the pull request.

element.name: Run the build and deployment pipeline
element.documentation: Build, package, scan, and promote a change through environments automatically, with gates that stop a failing build.

element.name: Scan code and dependencies for security defects
element.documentation: Run static, dependency, and secret scanning on every change and remediate findings within the applicable service level.

element.name: Manage technical debt
element.documentation: Record, size, and prioritize technical debt, and reserve capacity in each increment to retire it. Debt items live in the same backlog as features so the trade-off is visible at prioritization, not discovered at incident time.

element.name: Manage application configuration and feature flags
element.documentation: Control configuration and feature-flag changes so behavior can be changed or reverted without a code release, with an audit trail.

element.name: Support a production application
element.documentation: Diagnose and fix application defects escalated from service management, and feed root causes back into the backlog.

element.name: Decommission an application
element.documentation: Retire an application: migrate or archive its data to the retention schedule, remove interfaces and access, and update the inventory.

element.name: Capture and apply cardholder payment
element.documentation: Accept a cardholder payment through any channel and apply it to the account on the correct effective date.

element.name: Assign delinquency treatment strategy
element.documentation: Segment delinquent accounts and assign the contact and treatment strategy. Runs nightly after delinquency bucketing; the strategy drives queue, channel, intensity, and hardship routing, and a wrong assignment is a conduct risk as much as a loss risk.

element.name: Execute outbound collections contact
element.documentation: Execute outbound contact attempts within contact-frequency and communication constraints. Contact windows, frequency caps, and channel consent come from FDCPA, Reg F, and TCPA; the process starts at queue release and ends when the disposition is recorded.

element.name: Negotiate and administer payment arrangement
element.documentation: Agree, document, and administer a payment arrangement or settlement. Covers promises to pay, long-term arrangements, and settlements; terms must fit the approved matrix, and the arrangement drives bucket movement and interest treatment downstream.

element.name: Execute charge-off
element.documentation: Execute charge-off on policy timing and record the accounting effect. Timing follows the charge-off policy aligned to regulatory guidance; the entry moves the balance to charged-off status and hands the account to recovery placement.

element.name: Furnish credit bureau data
element.documentation: Compile and furnish account data to the consumer reporting agencies. Monthly Metro 2 furnishing to the bureaus; accuracy is an FCRA obligation, and the file must reconcile to the system of record before transmission.

element.name: Handle credit reporting dispute
element.documentation: Investigate and respond to a consumer credit reporting dispute within the required period. Direct and bureau-routed disputes both land here; FCRA sets the investigation window, and the outcome must correct both the bureau file and the account when the consumer is right.

element.name: Issue debt validation notice
element.documentation: Generate and deliver the required validation notice within the prescribed period. The validation notice is a statutory precondition to continued collection on affected accounts; timing and content mistakes surface directly as regulatory findings.

element.name: Assess and land regulatory change
element.documentation: Detect a regulatory change, assess applicability and impact, and drive implementation. Starts at horizon scanning and ends when the change is implemented and evidenced in the affected processes; applicability calls are documented even when the answer is not applicable.

element.name: Execute compliance monitoring test
element.documentation: Execute a scheduled control test and record the result and any exceptions. Runs the monitoring schedule agreed with the compliance plan; exceptions become issues in remediation tracking with owners and dates rather than emails.

element.name: Screen for sanctions and watchlists
element.documentation: Screen parties and transactions against sanctions and watchlists and adjudicate hits. Screening runs at onboarding and on list updates across cardholders, clients, and suppliers; a hit blocks processing until dispositioned, and the disposition is retained as evidence.

element.name: Investigate and file suspicious activity report
element.documentation: Investigate an alert and, where warranted, prepare and file the regulatory report. The SAR decision and filing run on the BSA clock from alert qualification; the investigation file must stand on its own for examiner review, and filing is confidential by law.

element.name: Analyze complaint signal for conduct risk
element.documentation: Aggregate and analyze complaint data for unfair or deceptive practice risk. Feeds the UDAAP program: complaint taxonomy, root cause, and trend analysis across channels, including complaints held by servicing clients about serviced portfolios.

element.name: Set and deploy credit decision strategy
element.documentation: Define, test, approve, and deploy changes to the credit decision strategy and its cutoffs. Strategy changes ship through champion-challenger testing with documented approval; the deployed strategy is the single decisioning authority for originations.

element.name: Develop and validate credit model
element.documentation: Build, document, and validate credit and fraud models prior to production deployment. Development evidence, data lineage, and validation results follow model risk management expectations; nothing reaches production without an independent validation record.

element.name: Execute credit line increase program
element.documentation: Identify eligible accounts and execute line increases under the approved strategy. Eligibility, ability-to-pay checks, and notice requirements are built into the program design; execution is batch with opt-out handling.

element.name: Execute credit line decrease or account action
element.documentation: Apply risk-driven line decreases or account actions, with required notice. Adverse action obligations apply to decreases and closures just as they do to declines; the notice must state the principal reasons and bureau information used.

element.name: Conduct monthly portfolio credit review
element.documentation: Review vintage, roll-rate, and segment performance against risk appetite and record the actions agreed at the portfolio credit review.

element.name: Produce loss forecast and allowance
element.documentation: Produce the credit loss forecast and set the allowance for the reporting period. The CECL forecast and allowance feed the financial statements; assumptions, overlays, and approvals are documented for both auditors and examiners.

element.name: Maintain authorization strategy
element.documentation: Define and deploy the rules governing real-time authorization decisions. Authorization strategy balances approval rates, fraud losses, and credit exposure in real time; changes deploy through the same testing discipline as origination strategy.

element.name: Perform account review and reissue decision
element.documentation: Review account risk periodically and decide reissue, close, or continue. Periodic account review drives reissue, line, and closure decisions at card expiry and on risk triggers; decisions carry the same notice obligations as any adverse action.

element.name: Acquire and refresh credit bureau data
element.documentation: Source consumer bureau data for prescreen, account review, and portfolio monitoring under permissible purpose, and manage refresh cadence and quality.

element.name: Handle cardholder inquiry
element.documentation: Receive, understand, and resolve a cardholder inquiry across any servicing channel. First-contact resolution is the design goal across phone, chat, and secure message; anything unresolved routes to a case with ownership and a promise date.

element.name: Ingest and integrate source data
element.documentation: Acquire, integrate, and land source data into the enterprise data platform. Ingestion lands source extracts into the platform with schema validation, lineage capture, and quality checks at the gate rather than downstream.

element.name: Deploy and monitor production model
element.documentation: Deploy an approved model to production and monitor its ongoing performance. Deployment follows model risk approval; monitoring covers drift, stability, and performance against the validation baseline, with retirement triggers agreed up front.

element.name: Onboard and classify data asset
element.documentation: Register a data asset, assign ownership, and classify it for handling. Onboarding assigns owner, steward, classification, and retention up front; the Collibra registration is the system of record this model's stub points at.

element.name: Measure and remediate data quality
element.documentation: Measure data quality against defined expectations and drive remediation. Quality rules run against critical data elements with published thresholds; breaches create remediation work with the data owner, not just a dashboard entry.

element.name: Publish metadata and lineage to catalog
element.documentation: Publish metadata, lineage, and ownership into the governance catalog. The catalog is where consumers discover data and its lineage; publication is part of change delivery, not an afterthought, so the catalog stays current by construction.

element.name: Execute records retention and disposition
element.documentation: Apply the retention schedule and execute defensible disposition of records. Disposition is defensible destruction: eligibility verified against holds, execution evidenced by certificate, and the retention schedule is the single authority.

element.name: Detect and bucket delinquent account
element.documentation: Identify accounts that have missed a payment and assign them to the correct delinquency bucket. Bucketing runs in the nightly cycle and is the trigger for every downstream collections treatment; a bucketing error propagates into contact, reporting, and accounting.

element.name: Enroll cardholder in digital servicing
element.documentation: Register and authenticate a cardholder for web and mobile self-service. Enrollment binds the cardholder to a verified identity with step-up options; weak enrollment is the account-takeover front door, so identity proofing follows the fraud strategy.

element.name: Serve digital self-service transaction
element.documentation: Execute a cardholder self-service action in web or mobile without agent involvement. Self-service actions execute against the same core services as agent actions, with the same entitlements; the channel changes, the control does not.

element.name: Process cardholder dispute claim
element.documentation: Take a cardholder dispute claim, apply provisional credit, investigate, determine, and notify within regulatory timers.

element.name: Execute network chargeback
element.documentation: Submit and track a chargeback through the network within the applicable filing window. Chargeback rights and filing windows differ by network and reason code; a missed window converts a recoverable dispute into an issuer loss.

element.name: Process representment and pre-arbitration
element.documentation: Evaluate merchant representment and pursue pre-arbitration where warranted. Representment evidence is weighed against the reason code requirements; pre-arbitration is pursued only where the economics and the evidence support it.

element.name: Finalize dispute determination and notify
element.documentation: Make the final dispute determination, adjust the account, and issue the compliant notice. The determination closes the Reg E or Reg Z clock: account adjustment, provisional credit disposition, and the written explanation must all land within the window.

element.name: Maintain target-state architecture and roadmap
element.documentation: Define and refresh the target state for each domain and the sequenced roadmap to reach it, aligned to the investment plan.

element.name: Review solution architecture for an initiative
element.documentation: Assess a proposed solution against standards, target state, and risk before funding and again before build; record the decision.

element.name: Grant or decline an architecture exception
element.documentation: Evaluate a request to deviate from a standard, set conditions and expiry, and track the exception to closure.

element.name: Maintain architecture standards and reference models
element.documentation: Author, review, version, and retire the standards and reference models that solution reviews are judged against.

element.name: Assess technology lifecycle and rationalization
element.documentation: Rate each application and platform for tolerate, invest, migrate, or eliminate; identify duplication and end-of-support exposure.

element.name: Maintain the capability map and process inventory
element.documentation: Keep the business architecture model current: harvest changes, run the quality gates, and publish the refreshed model to its consumers.

element.name: Assess change impact of a proposed system change
element.documentation: Trace a proposed system or interface change to the processes, capabilities, and clients it affects, and brief the change authority.

element.name: Evaluate and select a technology or platform
element.documentation: Run the evaluation for a new technology or vendor platform: requirements, options, proof of concept, and a recommendation into procurement.

element.name: Maintain the application and technology inventory
element.documentation: Keep the inventory of applications, platforms, and interfaces complete and attributed, including owner, tier, hosting, and lifecycle state.

element.name: Recognize interchange and servicing revenue
element.documentation: Calculate and recognize interchange, fee, and servicing revenue for the period. Revenue recognition follows the network and client contract terms; interchange, fees, and servicing revenue post to the ledger with support for audit.

element.name: Process supplier payment
element.documentation: Validate, approve, and execute payment to a supplier. Invoices match to contract and receipt before payment; approval limits and segregation of duties are the fraud controls the audit tests.

element.name: Detect and action transaction fraud alert
element.documentation: Detect a suspected fraudulent transaction, action the alert, and contact the cardholder. Alert handling runs against loss and customer-friction budgets; actions span block, reissue, and contact, and the clock matters because exposure grows per transaction.

element.name: Investigate and adjudicate fraud case
element.documentation: Investigate a suspected fraud case and reach a documented determination. The case determination separates true fraud from friendly fraud and abuse, drives the Reg E liability decision, and feeds the loss and strategy data.

element.name: Respond to account takeover event
element.documentation: Contain, remediate, and communicate an account takeover or identity compromise event. Account takeover response contains first, then remediates credentials, reverses fraudulent activity, and communicates with the cardholder; speed limits the loss.

element.name: Recover and write off fraud loss
element.documentation: Pursue recovery of fraud losses and write off the residual with correct accounting. Recovery pursues merchants, networks, and other issuers where rights exist; the residual writes off to the fraud loss line with the accounting evidenced.

element.name: Submit network fraud reporting
element.documentation: Compile and submit fraud reporting to the networks within required thresholds. Network fraud reporting (TC40, SAFE) has thresholds and deadlines; late or wrong reporting risks network compliance programs and fines.

element.name: Maintain fraud detection strategy
element.documentation: Define, test, and deploy changes to fraud detection rules and models. Strategy changes are tested against recent fraud and false-positive performance before deployment; every rule change is versioned and reversible.

element.name: Manage daily funding position
element.documentation: Determine, fund, and report the daily liquidity and funding position. The daily position covers settlement obligations, deposit flows, and contingency lines; a funding miss is a same-day escalation, not a report.

element.name: Execute monthly financial close
element.documentation: Complete the period-end close, including reconciliations, accruals, and reporting sign-off. The close calendar drives reconciliations, accruals, and sign-offs to the reporting deadline; open items age visibly and block sign-off past threshold.

element.name: Provision and certify access
element.documentation: Grant, review, and certify access to systems and data. Access follows least privilege with owner approval; the quarterly certification and automatic revocation of uncertified access are the controls CRI assesses.

element.name: Detect and respond to security event
element.documentation: Detect, investigate, contain, and remediate a security event. Detection through containment runs the incident playbook with severity-driven escalation; the timeline is evidence for both the CRI assessment and any notification duty.

element.name: Remediate vulnerability
element.documentation: Triage and remediate an identified vulnerability within the applicable service level. Severity sets the remediation SLA; breaches escalate rather than languish, and closure requires verification, not just a patch record.

element.name: Maintain cardholder data scope and evidence
element.documentation: Maintain the cardholder data environment scope and the supporting compliance evidence. PCI scope is maintained continuously: network segmentation, asset inventory, and evidence collection, so assessment is a report, not a scramble.

element.name: Post interchange and settlement entries
element.documentation: Calculate and post interchange and settlement accounting entries to the ledger. Interchange entries reconcile to network reports before posting; unexplained variances stop the post rather than flowing into revenue.

element.name: Build and permission prospect list
element.documentation: Source, screen, and permission prospect data for use in acquisition campaigns. Prospect data carries permissible-purpose and suppression obligations; the list that leaves this process is the compliant universe for everything downstream.

element.name: Construct and approve firm offer of credit
element.documentation: Define offer criteria and terms, and obtain compliance approval before release. A firm offer of credit commits the bank under FCRA; criteria, terms, and the compliance sign-off are locked before any channel sees the offer.

element.name: Execute acquisition campaign
element.documentation: Deploy the approved offer across selected channels and manage in-flight performance. In-flight management covers channel performance, budget, and suppression hygiene; changes to a live campaign re-enter compliance review when terms move.

element.name: Review marketing creative for compliance
element.documentation: Review creative, disclosures, and claims for regulatory adequacy before release. Review covers claims, disclosures, and UDAAP risk across every asset and channel; nothing ships without the documented sign-off this process exists to produce.

element.name: Review campaign performance and adjust targeting
element.documentation: Evaluate response, approval, and early vintage economics for in-flight campaigns and decide continue, adjust, or stop.

element.name: Reconcile network settlement
element.documentation: Reconcile network settlement files against internal transaction and ledger positions and resolve breaks.

element.name: Capture card application
element.documentation: Accept and validate a complete card application from any origination channel. Capture is complete when the application has every field decisioning needs and the applicant has the required disclosures; incomplete applications route to cure, not decline.

element.name: Verify applicant identity and satisfy CIP
element.documentation: Verify the applicant's identity and record evidence satisfying customer identification obligations. CIP evidence is retained per BSA requirements; verification failures route to document request rather than automatic decline, and synthetic identity signals feed fraud screening.

element.name: Screen application for fraud
element.documentation: Score and adjudicate the application for synthetic, stolen, and first-party fraud risk. Fraud screening runs before credit decisioning so stolen and synthetic identities never consume a bureau pull; referred applications go to manual review with an SLA.

element.name: Execute credit decision
element.documentation: Apply the approved credit strategy to render an approve, decline, or counter-offer decision with a line assignment.

element.name: Issue adverse action notice
element.documentation: Generate and deliver a compliant adverse action or counter-offer notice within the required period. ECOA and FCRA set the notice content and the clock; the principal reasons must match the actual decision factors, which is exactly what fair-lending testing checks.

element.name: Establish account and issue credentials
element.documentation: Open the account on the core platform and issue the card credential. Account establishment writes the account of record and triggers credential issuance; a failure here strands an approved applicant, which is why it carries a same-day SLA.

element.name: Manage card production and fulfillment
element.documentation: Oversee vendor-executed card personalization, production, and delivery, including inventory, service levels, and exception handling.

element.name: Provision credential to digital wallet
element.documentation: Provision the card credential into a digital wallet or tokenized environment. Wallet provisioning runs the network token flows with step-up verification where risk requires; weak provisioning is a known fraud vector the strategy watches.

element.name: Handle application withdrawal and abandonment
element.documentation: Manage applications withdrawn by the applicant or abandoned before completion. Withdrawn and abandoned applications still carry notice, retention, and bureau obligations; this process closes them compliantly instead of letting them age.

element.name: Fulfill issuing bank oversight obligations
element.documentation: Produce contracted reporting, respond to oversight requests, and manage obligations under the issuing bank agreement.

element.name: Process authorization request
element.documentation: Receive, decision, and respond to a real-time authorization request within the network response window.

element.name: Ingest clearing file and post transactions
element.documentation: Receive network clearing files and post transactions to cardholder accounts. Clearing ingestion matches presentments to authorizations, posts to accounts, and routes exceptions; the file must balance to network totals before posting completes.

element.name: Process returned payment and assess NSF
element.documentation: Handle returned and reversed payments and assess the associated fees. Return handling reverses the payment application, restores the balance, assesses any permitted fee, and feeds NSF patterns to risk; Reg E error claims can start here.

element.name: Manage token and credential lifecycle
element.documentation: Issue, update, suspend, and delete payment tokens and credentials. Token lifecycle events flow between networks, wallets, and the account of record; a stale token strands the cardholder's wallet, so lifecycle sync is monitored.

element.name: Implement network mandate release
element.documentation: Assess and implement network mandate and release changes by the required date. Network mandates carry hard effective dates and fines for misses; assessment, build, and attestation are tracked per mandate from bulletin to production.

element.name: Fulfill consumer privacy request
element.documentation: Receive, verify, and fulfill a consumer privacy rights request within the required period. Identity verification precedes any disclosure; state privacy laws set the clocks and the evidence of fulfillment is retained per request.

element.name: Design and approve product change
element.documentation: Define, price, and obtain approval for a change to a card product. A product change binds pricing, terms, and eligibility; approval spans product, credit, finance, legal, and compliance before configuration starts.

element.name: Author and version disclosure
element.documentation: Author, review, approve, and version cardholder agreements and disclosures. Agreements and disclosures are versioned with effective dates; every account references the version it was disclosed under, which is what makes remediation tractable.

element.name: Launch product to market
element.documentation: Configure, test, and release a product for origination across all affected systems. Launch is a coordinated configuration across origination, core, servicing, and statements, verified in test before the product opens to volume.

element.name: Retire or migrate product
element.documentation: Sunset a product and migrate affected accounts with required notice. Retirement manages the migration and notices for live accounts; terms changes ride the change-in-terms rules, and the product stays resolvable for history.

element.name: Plan the test strategy for a release
element.documentation: Decide scope, risk-based depth, environments, data, and entry and exit criteria for a release before build starts.

element.name: Build and maintain the automated regression suite
element.documentation: Author, review, and prune automated tests so the regression suite stays fast, trusted, and aligned to current behavior.

element.name: Execute functional and regression testing
element.documentation: Run planned functional tests and the regression suite against a candidate build, and record results against the plan.

element.name: Execute performance and resilience testing
element.documentation: Load, soak, and failover-test a candidate against stated capacity and recovery objectives before a material release.

element.name: Run user acceptance testing with the business
element.documentation: Prepare scripts and data, run acceptance with business owners, and obtain their sign-off or documented rejection.

element.name: Manage defects to closure
element.documentation: Triage, prioritize, assign, and verify defects found in test or production, and report defect trends by area.

element.name: Provision test environments and masked data
element.documentation: Stand up and refresh non-production environments with representative, masked data, and retire them on schedule.

element.name: Certify a release for production
element.documentation: Assess test results, open defects, and exit criteria, and issue or withhold the quality certification the change authority relies on.

element.name: Verify a release in production
element.documentation: Run post-deployment checks and smoke tests in production, confirm monitoring is green, and trigger rollback if criteria fail.

element.name: Place account with collection agency
element.documentation: Select, place, and monitor charged-off accounts with an external collection agency. Agency placement follows the approved network with performance and conduct oversight; the agency acts in the bank's name, so its conduct is the bank's risk.

element.name: Execute debt sale
element.documentation: Assemble, price, and execute a sale of charged-off receivables. Debt sale packages carry account-level data quality and documentation warranties; buyer diligence and post-sale complaint routing are part of the process, not after-thoughts.

element.name: Handle bankruptcy notification
element.documentation: Receive, verify, and action a bankruptcy notification with required account treatment. The automatic stay stops collection on notice; verification, claim filing, and account treatment follow bankruptcy chapter rules with dates that are court deadlines.

element.name: Handle deceased cardholder and estate
element.documentation: Verify a deceased notification and manage the account through estate resolution. Estate handling balances recovery with conduct: verified notification stops collection contact, and the claim proceeds through the estate at the estate's pace.

element.name: Post recovery and account for proceeds
element.documentation: Post recoveries and account for proceeds from agency, legal, and sale channels. Proceeds post against charged-off balances with channel attribution; recoveries feed the loss forecast, so mis-posting distorts the allowance.

element.name: Prepare regulatory reporting data
element.documentation: Assemble, validate, and certify the data supporting regulatory reporting submissions. Report data is assembled from governed sources with reconciliation to the ledger and prior submissions; certification is a named officer's sign-off, not a batch job.

element.name: Accrue rewards earn
element.documentation: Calculate and post rewards earn to the rewards ledger for qualifying activity. Earn accrues per the program terms with promotional multipliers; the accrual creates the liability finance reconciles, so earn rules and accounting stay in lockstep.

element.name: Process rewards redemption
element.documentation: Execute a cardholder rewards redemption and settle the resulting obligation. Redemption executes across cash, statement credit, and partner channels; partner settlement follows the program contract, and failed redemptions reverse cleanly.

element.name: Reconcile rewards liability
element.documentation: Reconcile the rewards ledger to the recorded liability and resolve differences. The rewards liability reconciliation catches earn, redemption, and expiry drift between the ledger and finance; differences are investigated, not plugged.

element.name: Manage issue and remediation to closure
element.documentation: Track an identified issue through remediation to evidenced closure. Issues from any source (audit, compliance, self-identified, exam) run one lifecycle: owner, action plan, dates, and evidenced closure that survives challenge.

element.name: Validate model independently
element.documentation: Perform independent validation of a model and record the outcome and conditions. Independent validation is organizationally separate from development; findings condition or block production use, and revalidation triggers are set at approval.

element.name: Coordinate regulatory examination
element.documentation: Coordinate the response to a regulatory examination, including evidence and findings. Exam coordination controls the single flow of requests, evidence, and meetings; every submission is logged and consistent with what other responses have said.

element.name: Assess interest, fees, and minimum payment
element.documentation: Calculate interest, fees, and the minimum payment due for the billing cycle. Cycle assessment applies the cardholder agreement exactly: interest method, fee triggers, and minimum-payment formula, because a systematic error here is a remediation event.

element.name: Deliver and archive statement
element.documentation: Deliver the statement by the cardholder's elected channel and retain it for retrieval. Delivery honors the e-consent election and postal fallback; the archived statement is the legal record retrieved for disputes and subpoenas.

element.name: Process billing adjustment or goodwill credit
element.documentation: Apply approved goodwill credits, fee reversals, and billing corrections. Adjustments carry approval limits and reason codes; patterns feed complaint and conduct analysis because repeated goodwill on the same defect is a signal.

element.name: Execute account maintenance request
element.documentation: Execute a cardholder-requested change to account details or preferences. Maintenance changes execute after authentication with an audit trail; address changes get extra scrutiny because they precede takeover fraud.

element.name: Authenticate cardholder
element.documentation: Authenticate a cardholder to policy before disclosing information or executing a change. Authentication strength scales with request risk; failures route to step-up rather than disclosure, and the policy is tuned with the fraud team.

element.name: Capture and resolve complaint
element.documentation: Capture, classify, resolve, and evidence a cardholder complaint. Complaint handling runs intake through evidenced resolution with regulatory routing where required; the taxonomy feeds UDAAP analysis, so classification is not clerical.

element.name: Generate and deliver required notice
element.documentation: Generate and deliver a regulatory or contractual notice to the cardholder. Notice generation is driven by account events with content owned by legal and compliance; proof of delivery and version are retained per notice.

element.name: Enroll account in hardship or assistance program
element.documentation: Assess eligibility and enroll an account into a hardship or payment assistance program. Hardship enrollment applies documented eligibility consistently; program terms change interest, fees, and reporting, so enrollment is evidenced and reviewed.

element.name: Maintain servicing knowledge content
element.documentation: Author, review, and publish agent-facing knowledge and guidance. Knowledge content is the agent's authority in the moment; review cadence and ownership keep it aligned with policy, because stale guidance becomes wrong answers at scale.

element.name: Monitor and score servicing interactions
element.documentation: Sample, monitor, score, and calibrate servicing interactions for quality and regulatory compliance signal.

element.name: Administer secured card deposit lifecycle
element.documentation: Collect, hold, apply, and refund security deposits for secured card accounts, including graduation and charge-off application, with correct accounting and disclosure treatment.

element.name: Apply servicemember and military lending protections
element.documentation: Identify covered borrowers, apply the required rate and fee protections, and evidence compliance for servicemember accounts.

element.name: Fund daily network settlement position
element.documentation: Determine and fund the daily settlement position with the networks. The settlement position must fund by the network deadline in the settlement currency; a miss is a network compliance event, so the process carries same-day escalation.

element.name: Reconcile cash and suspense accounts
element.documentation: Reconcile cash and suspense account positions and clear aged items. Cash and suspense reconcile daily with aging visible; suspense is a control account, and items that age past threshold escalate to investigation.

element.name: Investigate and clear settlement exception
element.documentation: Investigate settlement breaks and exceptions and drive them to resolution. Settlement exceptions are worked to root cause across network reports, the gateway, and the ledger; recurring breaks feed a fix, not a workaround.

element.name: Monitor and optimize interchange qualification
element.documentation: Monitor interchange qualification rates, identify downgrades, and drive corrections in processing configuration.

element.name: Cut cycle and generate statement
element.documentation: Cut the billing cycle and generate the cardholder statement including the rewards position. Cycle cut is the hard deadline that sequences assessment, statement generation, and delivery; a late cut cascades into payment due dates and regulatory timing.

element.name: Evaluate and execute portfolio transaction
element.documentation: Assess, diligence, price, and execute the acquisition or sale of a card portfolio, through to hand-off into conversion.

element.name: Deliver software change
element.documentation: Design, build, test, and release a software change into production. The umbrella delivery flow from approved demand to production release; the engineering-level decomposition lives in the P-APPDEV and P-QE processes it coordinates.

element.name: Respond to service incident
element.documentation: Detect, triage, resolve, and review a service incident. Incident response runs detect, triage, resolve, and review with severity-driven communication; customer-impacting incidents feed problem management and the resilience picture.

element.name: Execute disaster recovery test
element.documentation: Plan and execute a recovery test against committed recovery objectives. The annual test exercises recovery against committed RTO and RPO with business participation; misses become tracked remediation, and the evidence supports the CRI assessment.

element.name: Onboard and operate integration
element.documentation: Design, register, and operate an interface between systems. Integration onboarding registers the interface, its data, and its owners before traffic flows; unregistered interfaces are how impact analysis goes blind.

element.name: Configure client program
element.documentation: Configure platform, product, treatment, and reporting for a new client program. Program configuration translates the client contract into platform, product, treatment, and reporting settings; every setting traces to a contract clause or a documented default.

element.name: Convert client portfolio
element.documentation: Migrate a client portfolio onto the servicing platform with reconciled balances and no cardholder disruption.

element.name: Deconvert client portfolio
element.documentation: Migrate a client portfolio off the servicing platform and hand over records. Deconversion hands a portfolio off with data, documents, and cutover timing per contract; the obligation to do it well survives the relationship ending.

element.name: Produce contracted client reporting
element.documentation: Produce and deliver reporting to the schedule and specification in the client contract. Contracted reporting ships to specification and schedule; late or wrong reporting is an SLA breach with credits, so production is monitored like any critical batch.

element.name: Exchange client data feed
element.documentation: Send and receive contracted data feeds with the client on schedule. Data feeds run both directions on contracted schedules with schema and quality checks at the boundary; feed failures page, because clients reconcile against them.

element.name: Bill client servicing fees
element.documentation: Calculate and invoice servicing fees per the contract and recognize the revenue. Fee billing calculates from contracted schedules against actual volumes; invoices carry the detail clients audit, and revenue recognition follows the contract.

element.name: Support client audit or examination
element.documentation: Assemble evidence and respond to client and client-regulator oversight requests. Client audits and client-regulator exams get coordinated evidence with the same discipline as the bank's own exams; commitments made in responses are tracked.

element.name: Intake and deliver client-directed change
element.documentation: Receive, price, approve, and deliver a change requested by a servicing client. Client-directed changes are priced, approved, and delivered under the contract's change provisions; scope discipline here is what keeps serviced portfolios profitable.

element.name: Onboard and diligence supplier
element.documentation: Assess, diligence, and contract a new supplier with required security and risk terms. Due diligence is risk-tiered per the TPRM policy; no supplier touches cardholder data before security review and contract terms land, which is the EX.DD control.

element.name: Monitor supplier risk and performance
element.documentation: Monitor supplier risk, performance, and service levels through the relationship. Ongoing monitoring covers risk, performance, and financial condition on a tier-driven cadence; findings route to the relationship owner with dates.

element.name: Execute supplier exit
element.documentation: Execute the exit of a supplier, including data return and service transition. Exit executes the termination plan: service transition, data return or destruction with certificate, and access revocation, proving the exit clause was real.

element.name: Card Authorization
element.documentation: A card presented at a merchant, authorized or declined inside the scheme timeout. The tightest latency budget in the estate, and the reason the screening call has a circuit breaker rather than a retry.

element.name: Dispute and Chargeback
element.documentation: A cardholder disputes a transaction. Raised in the contact center, handled in the vendor platform, settled back through the ledger.

element.name: Installment Loan Application
element.documentation: An applicant applies for point-of-sale credit. Bureau search, affordability and a decision, with referral to an underwriter when the automated decision declines to take it.

element.name: Regulatory Return
element.documentation: The monthly supervisory return. Entirely batch, and the only flow whose deadline is external and non-negotiable.

element.name: Card Servicing
element.documentation: Self-service balance, statement, limit and payment servicing for cardholders.

element.name: Collections Workspace
element.documentation: Agent workspace for arrears treatment and payment arrangements.

element.name: Customer 360
element.documentation: Curated single view of the customer for analytics and servicing.

element.name: Dispute Management
element.documentation: Chargeback and dispute handling, bought rather than built.

element.name: Customer Identity Service
element.documentation: Authentication, session and identity proofing for every customer channel.

element.name: Identity Document Verification
element.documentation: Document and liveness verification at onboarding, bought rather than built. The identity service sends the captured document and selfie; the vendor calls back with the result. Restricted from the first byte, so the path to the vendor is private.

element.name: Installment Lending
element.documentation: Point-of-sale installment lending. New product, onboarding onto the AWS landing zone in eu-west-2, integrating with the existing card ledger for disbursement and with the warehouse for regulatory reporting.

element.name: Lending Portfolio Performance
element.documentation: Arrears, roll rates, vintage curves and payment behavior for point-of-sale finance, curated nightly from the product's own events into BigQuery and served to the lending analysts through Looker. The first data product on the Google Cloud side, in an analytics project of its own.

element.name: Merchant Portal
element.documentation: Where a merchant applies for an account, sees settlements and chargebacks, and downloads statements. Built in-house on the Azure landing zone, beside Rewards Redemption; the first product assembled from parts rather than built on a shape.

element.name: Open Banking Affordability
element.documentation: Affordability assessment from the shopper's own bank data, with consent, in the seconds a point-of-sale decision has. Bought rather than built; the vendor runs the open banking connections and the categorization, we send the consent and receive the assessment. Restricted from the first byte, so the path to the vendor is private.

element.name: Point-of-Sale Finance
element.documentation: Financing offered at a retailer's checkout. The dealer or merchant starts the application in their own system, the shopper completes it on their phone, and the decision comes back before the sale closes. Built in-house on the Google Cloud landing zone, the first product to land there.

element.name: Rewards Redemption
element.documentation: Cardholders browse the rewards catalog and redeem points for statement credit, gift cards and merchandise. Built in-house on the Azure landing zone; a redemption is confirmed in the response and fulfilled afterward by a worker consuming the product's own events.

element.name: NICE Actimize Screening
element.documentation: Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, bought rather than built. Called in line by the authorization switch at transaction time, with a nightly rescreen of the book and a return feed for reconciliation and model risk.

element.name: Prospect to Funded Account
element.documentation: A qualified applicant receives an actionable credit decision quickly and compliantly, and can transact within days.

element.name: Merchant Signed to Settled
element.documentation: A merchant — usually brought by an ISO — is underwritten, boarded, and sponsored into the networks, can accept cards, and is settled daily with exposure managed.

element.name: Dealer Purchase to Funded Loan
element.documentation: A consumer buying an RV, boat, or powersports vehicle gets a financing decision at the dealer while they are standing there, and the dealer is funded within days.

element.name: Deposit Opened to Maturity
element.documentation: A saver opens a CD or savings account — directly or through a broker — funds it without friction, and is paid accurately at maturity. This stream is also how the bank funds its lending.

element.name: Concept to Market
element.documentation: A product change reaches market correctly disclosed, correctly priced, and correctly configured everywhere it needs to be.

element.name: Client Opportunity to Live Program
element.documentation: A client institution's portfolio moves onto our servicing platform with no cardholder disruption and full regulatory continuity.

element.name: Delinquency to Recovery
element.documentation: Accounts in difficulty are treated fairly and consistently, and the enterprise recovers what it reasonably can.

element.name: Inquiry to Resolution
element.documentation: A cardholder with a problem gets a correct, timely answer and, where money is involved, gets it back within regulatory timers.

element.name: Transact to Statement
element.documentation: Transactions are authorized reliably, posted accurately, billed correctly, and paid without friction.

element.name: Onboard the identity verification vendor
element.documentation: Buy document and liveness verification rather than build it: the vendor tenancy, the gateway, the private path to the vendor, and the webhook listener that hands results back to the identity service.

element.name: Build installment lending on AWS
element.documentation: Stand up the installment lending product on the AWS landing zone: the edge and load balancer, the web and API tiers, the database, the object store, the async worker and the integration hub that fronts the ledger, the bureau and the CRM.

element.name: Curate lending performance in BigQuery
element.documentation: The first data product on the Google Cloud side: point-of-sale finance's events curated nightly into BigQuery in an analytics project of its own, served through Looker and registered in Collibra. The second workload project on the hub, so the product's tenancy and its analytics tenancy are separate.

element.name: Assemble the merchant portal on Azure
element.documentation: The merchant portal from the library's parts: the API, the web channel, the datastore, the event publisher, and the onboarding analyst role the product creates. Assembled as one product file with no shape; the landing zone answers for the gateway, the cluster, the database and the bus.

element.name: Buy affordability data for point-of-sale finance
element.documentation: Open banking affordability from TrueLayer, reached over Private Service Connect from the lending project on Google Cloud and returning its assessment by webhook: the vendor shape's private path and webhook return, resolved against Google Cloud for the first time. Our side is a gateway, an egress and a listener beside the point-of-sale API.

element.name: Land point-of-sale finance on Google Cloud
element.documentation: The first product on the Google Cloud landing zone: the API, the web channel, the datastore and the event publisher of the digital shape, resolved against GKE, Apigee, Cloud SQL and Pub/Sub. The dealer integrations that start an application already run through Apigee, so the product lands beside its partners.

element.name: Stand up the regulatory reporting engine
element.documentation: Replace the spreadsheet-based return with an engine sourcing from the warehouse, and extend the customer semantic layer with the fields the return needs.

element.name: Build rewards redemption on Azure
element.documentation: The first product on the Azure digital shape: the catalog and redemption web front end and API, the product datastore, the event publisher, and the worker that fulfills a redemption after the response. Balances stay with the proposed rewards ledger; this is the channel in front of it.

element.name: Onboard the screening vendor
element.documentation: Buy sanctions and adverse-media screening rather than build it: the vendor tenant, the integration gateway, the private egress path and the identity federation, plus the change to the authorization switch that calls it.

element.name: Build installment lending on AWS rather than on-premises
element.documentation: Whether the new product goes onto the AWS landing zone or onto the existing on-premises estate the card systems run on.

element.name: Buy sanctions screening rather than build it
element.documentation: Whether to extend the fraud platform with sanctions and adverse-media screening or to onboard a vendor product for it.

element.name: Fold the card servicing datastore into the lending database
element.documentation: Whether the card servicing operational datastore should be retired into the new lending database once lending is live, rather than run as a second operational store for the same customers.

element.name: Buy identity document verification rather than build it
element.documentation: Whether to extend the identity service with document capture and liveness checking or to onboard a vendor for it.

element.name: Build rewards redemption on the Azure product shape
element.documentation: Whether to add redemption to the card servicing product or to build it as its own product on the Azure digital shape, the first to sit on it.

element.name: Assemble the merchant portal from parts rather than a shape
element.documentation: Whether a merchant-facing product needs a shape of its own before it is built, or can be assembled from the parts the digital shapes share and earn a shape when a second one follows.

element.name: Land the first product on Google Cloud
element.documentation: Whether a third cloud is worth a landing zone of its own for one product, or the product should land on Azure beside the other digital products and reach its dealer partners over the internet.

element.name: Buy affordability data on open banking rails
element.documentation: Whether point-of-sale finance assesses affordability from the shopper's own bank data, bought from an open banking vendor, or from the bureau data the installment lending product already uses.

element.name: Curate Google Cloud data on Google Cloud
element.documentation: Whether point-of-sale finance's performance data is curated in BigQuery beside the product, or carried to the enterprise warehouse on the Azure side the way every other data product is.

element.name: Periodic access certification
element.documentation: Access to systems handling cardholder data is re-certified by the owning manager on a fixed cycle; uncertified access is revoked.

element.name: Adverse action notice completeness
element.documentation: Every declined application generates a compliant adverse action notice with the principal reasons, within the required period.

element.name: Application completeness and disclosure
element.documentation: Applications are complete and required disclosures delivered before decisioning; incomplete files route to cure with notice-of-incompleteness timing honored.

element.name: Authorization availability and stand-in
element.documentation: Authorization availability is monitored against the network SLA with tested stand-in arrangements; incidents invoke the resilience playbook.

element.name: Cardholder authentication to policy
element.documentation: Cardholder authentication meets the risk-tiered policy before disclosure or account change, across every servicing channel.

element.name: Bureau furnishing accuracy
element.documentation: Furnished tradeline data is reconciled to the system of record before transmission; consumer disputes update furnishing.

element.name: Charge-off timing to policy
element.documentation: Charge-off executes at the policy timing aligned to regulatory guidance, with exceptions approved and documented.

element.name: Production change approval
element.documentation: No change reaches production without an approved change record, test evidence, and a rollback plan; emergency changes are reviewed after the fact.

element.name: Client reporting and feed monitoring
element.documentation: Contracted client reporting and data feeds are monitored to schedule and specification; misses alert before the client notices and count against the SLA.

element.name: Close reconciliation sign-off
element.documentation: Period-end reconciliations and journal approvals complete with segregation of duties before financial sign-off.

element.name: Complaint regulatory routing
element.documentation: Complaints are classified to taxonomy, resolved to SLA, and routed to regulators where required; executive and regulator complaints carry expedited handling.

element.name: Collections contact limits
element.documentation: Outbound contact respects time-of-day, frequency, and channel-consent constraints; blocked numbers and cease requests are honored.

element.name: Conversion balance and record verification
element.documentation: Portfolio conversions verify record counts, balances, and regulatory continuity before and after cutover, with client sign-off at each gate.

element.name: Cycle assessment validation
element.documentation: Interest, fee, and minimum-payment computation is validated against the cardholder agreement on every pricing or product change, and sampled each cycle.

element.name: Daily settlement and clearing reconciliation
element.documentation: Network settlement, clearing files, and interchange postings reconcile to network totals daily; unreconciled variances stop downstream posting.

element.name: Ingestion data quality gate
element.documentation: Source ingestion enforces schema and quality thresholds at the boundary; failing loads quarantine rather than land.

element.name: Recovery test against committed objectives
element.documentation: Recovery is exercised at least annually against stated RTO/RPO; misses produce tracked remediation.

element.name: Statutory collections notices
element.documentation: Validation and other statutory notices issue within the prescribed period with content owned by legal; continued collection is blocked until issued.

element.name: Fraud alert handling service level
element.documentation: Fraud alerts are actioned within the loss-budget SLA with disposition quality sampling; Reg E liability decisions are documented per case.

element.name: Settlement funding confirmation
element.documentation: The daily funding position is confirmed funded by the network deadline with dual verification and same-day escalation on a miss.

element.name: Security incident response execution
element.documentation: Security events run the incident response playbook with severity-driven escalation and post-incident review; the timeline is evidence.

element.name: Masked data outside production
element.documentation: Non-production environments carry masked or synthetic data; unmasked extracts require a time-boxed exception.

element.name: Furnishing and bucketing reconciliation
element.documentation: Delinquency bucketing and bureau furnishing reconcile to the system of record each cycle; unexplained movement blocks the file.

element.name: Marketing material compliance review
element.documentation: No creative or offer reaches market without documented compliance sign-off.

element.name: Notice content and delivery evidence
element.documentation: Required notices use legal-owned templates with version control, and delivery evidence is retained per notice.

element.name: Cardholder data scope and evidence maintenance
element.documentation: CDE scope, segmentation, and assessment evidence are maintained continuously against the PCI DSS requirement set.

element.name: Payment posting timeliness
element.documentation: Cardholder payments post as of the day of receipt per Reg Z crediting rules, with cutoff disclosures honored and exceptions reported.

element.name: Consumer privacy request fulfillment
element.documentation: Access and deletion requests are verified, fulfilled, and evidenced within the applicable statutory window.

element.name: Regulatory change implementation tracking
element.documentation: Applicability decisions and implementation actions for regulatory changes are tracked to evidenced completion with compliance sign-off.

element.name: Dispute acknowledgment timeliness
element.documentation: Written acknowledgment of an error claim is issued within the regulatory window; the timer starts at claim receipt, not triage.

element.name: Dispute determination timeliness and notice
element.documentation: Final dispute determinations, account adjustment, and the written explanation complete within the Reg E / Reg Z window; the clock is measured from claim receipt.

element.name: Provisional credit within regulatory window
element.documentation: Provisional credit is applied within the Reg E window when investigation extends past it, and collection on the disputed amount is suspended.

element.name: Regulatory report certification
element.documentation: Regulatory submissions reconcile to the ledger and prior filings and carry a named officer certification before transmission.

element.name: Retention schedule enforcement
element.documentation: Records are retained to schedule and destroyed on expiry with a certificate of disposition.

element.name: Sanctions and watchlist screening
element.documentation: Parties are screened at onboarding and on list updates; hits are dispositioned before processing continues.

element.name: Suspicious activity investigation and filing
element.documentation: Alerts are investigated and SARs filed within the statutory window, with supporting documentation retained.

element.name: Servicemember protections screening
element.documentation: SCRA and MLA eligibility is screened at origination and on notification, with rate and protection application evidenced.

element.name: Third-party due diligence before onboarding
element.documentation: No supplier processes cardholder data before risk-tiered due diligence is complete and accepted.

element.name: Treatment strategy approval
element.documentation: Collections treatment strategies and authorization strategies deploy only with documented risk and compliance approval and champion-challenger evidence.

element.name: Vulnerability remediation service level
element.documentation: Vulnerabilities are remediated within the SLA for their severity; breaches of the SLA are escalated and tracked.

element.name: Application Load Balancer
element.documentation: Terminates TLS and routes to the application tier.

element.name: Amazon API Gateway
element.documentation: The managed front door every AWS-hosted API is published through.

element.name: Amazon Bedrock
element.documentation: Managed access to foundation models (Amazon Nova, Claude, Llama and others) inside the account's own data boundary.

element.name: Amazon CloudFront and WAF
element.documentation: Edge distribution and the web application firewall in front of it.

element.name: Amazon CloudWatch
element.documentation: Metrics, logs and alarms for every workload in the landing zone.

element.name: Amazon EKS
element.documentation: Managed Kubernetes running the containerized workloads.

element.name: AWS KMS
element.documentation: Customer managed keys for data at rest.

element.name: Amazon MSK
element.documentation: Managed Kafka carrying domain events between products.

element.name: AWS Organizations
element.documentation: Account vending, service control policies and consolidated billing.

element.name: AWS PrivateLink
element.documentation: Private egress to partner and vendor endpoints without internet transit.

element.name: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
element.documentation: Managed relational database, Multi-AZ, encrypted with a customer managed key.

element.name: Amazon S3
element.documentation: Object storage for landing zones, artifacts and archives.

element.name: AWS Secrets Manager
element.documentation: Application credentials and rotation.

element.name: Amazon SQS
element.documentation: Managed queues between a product's own services, where a message is owed to one consumer rather than published to any.

element.name: AWS Transit Gateway
element.documentation: Hub for VPC-to-VPC and hybrid routing back to the data center.

element.name: Azure Kubernetes Service
element.documentation: Managed Kubernetes hosting the containerized estate.

element.name: Azure API Management
element.documentation: The API gateway every internal and partner API is published through.

element.name: Azure Event Hubs
element.documentation: Managed event streaming carrying a product's domain events to the workers that consume them.

element.name: Microsoft Foundry
element.documentation: Managed access to foundation models (OpenAI, Microsoft MAI, Claude and others), formerly Azure OpenAI Service and Azure AI Foundry.

element.name: Azure Key Vault
element.documentation: Secret, key and certificate management.

element.name: Azure Monitor
element.documentation: Metrics, logs and alerts for the Azure-hosted estate.

element.name: Azure Private Link
element.documentation: Private endpoints to bought services, so the only path our data takes to a vendor never touches the public internet.

element.name: Azure Service Bus
element.documentation: Enterprise messaging backbone for domain events.

element.name: Azure SQL Database
element.documentation: Managed relational database for operational datastores.

element.name: Azure Virtual WAN hub
element.documentation: The hub every virtual network attaches to, and the route back to the data center.

element.name: Card Servicing Backup and recovery
element.documentation: Copies that survive the thing they came from. The recovery objective is a property of this, not of the database.

element.name: Card Servicing Cache
element.documentation: In-memory key-value store. Also, in most estates, an accidental database with no backup.

element.name: Card Servicing DNS
element.documentation: Name resolution and, in practice, the failover mechanism of last resort.

element.name: Card Servicing Web application firewall
element.documentation: Request inspection at the edge. Blocks the traffic nobody wrote a test for.

element.name: Collections Workspace Backup and recovery
element.documentation: Copies that survive the thing they came from. The recovery objective is a property of this, not of the database.

element.name: Collections Workspace Cache
element.documentation: In-memory key-value store. Also, in most estates, an accidental database with no backup.

element.name: Collections Workspace DNS
element.documentation: Name resolution and, in practice, the failover mechanism of last resort.

element.name: Collections Workspace Web application firewall
element.documentation: Request inspection at the edge. Blocks the traffic nobody wrote a test for.

element.name: Collibra
element.documentation: Governance catalog and the intended system of record for metadata.

element.name: Microsoft Entra ID
element.documentation: Workforce and customer identity provider.

element.name: Apigee
element.documentation: The API gateway every internal and partner API on Google Cloud is published through; dealer and merchant integrations terminate here.

element.name: Backup and DR Service
element.documentation: Scheduled backups of the datastores and disks in the zone, retained in a second region.

element.name: BigQuery
element.documentation: Serverless warehouse; one dataset per data product, customer-managed keys, authorized views for the semantic layer.

element.name: Cloud Armor
element.documentation: Web application firewall and DDoS protection in front of every external load balancer.

element.name: Cloud CDN
element.documentation: Edge caching for the static parts of a product's channel, in front of the external load balancer.

element.name: Cloud DNS
element.documentation: Public and private zones for the Google Cloud estate, peered to the data center's resolvers.

element.name: Cloud Load Balancing
element.documentation: Global external and regional internal load balancers; the external ones carry Cloud Armor.

element.name: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
element.documentation: Managed PostgreSQL with regional high availability, the product datastore of the zone.

element.name: Cloud Composer
element.documentation: Managed Airflow, the schedule a data product's jobs run on.

element.name: Dataflow
element.documentation: Managed batch and streaming jobs, the curation engine of a data product on this side.

element.name: Cloud Storage
element.documentation: Object storage, one bucket per product with uniform access and customer-managed keys.

element.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
element.documentation: Managed access to foundation models (Gemini, Gemma, Claude and others) through Model Garden, formerly Vertex AI.

element.name: Google Kubernetes Engine
element.documentation: Managed Kubernetes for the containerized estate on Google Cloud, an Autopilot cluster per workload project.

element.name: Cloud Interconnect
element.documentation: Dedicated Interconnect back to the data center, two attachments in two edge availability domains; the failover between them is tested quarterly.

element.name: Cloud KMS
element.documentation: Customer-managed encryption keys for every datastore in the zone, one key ring per workload project.

element.name: Looker
element.documentation: The governed semantic layer and the dashboards over BigQuery.

element.name: Managed Service for Apache Kafka
element.documentation: Ordered, replayable event streams for the products that need to re-read what happened; the stream kind of the landing zone.

element.name: Memorystore for Redis
element.documentation: Managed Redis for the session and lookup caches a product keeps beside its datastore.

element.name: Cloud Monitoring
element.documentation: Metrics, logs and traces for everything in the organization, the Cloud Operations suite scoped per workload project.

element.name: Network Connectivity Center
element.documentation: The hub the workload VPC spokes and the interconnect attach to; the transit of the Google Cloud zone.

element.name: Private Service Connect
element.documentation: Private endpoints to Google services and to vendors who publish one, so nothing of ours reaches them over the internet.

element.name: Pub/Sub
element.documentation: The enterprise bus on Google Cloud, topics and subscriptions with at-least-once delivery; the queue kind of the landing zone.

element.name: Secret Manager
element.documentation: Application secrets, read by workload identity rather than by key.

element.name: Shared VPC network
element.documentation: The host project's network the workload projects attach to, with the tiers as subnetworks.

element.name: Lending External Load Balancer
element.documentation: The external HTTPS load balancer in front of the product's channel, with Cloud Armor attached; the edge of the lending workload on Google Cloud.

element.name: HA VPN
element.documentation: The backup path to the data center: HA VPN over the internet, two tunnels with BGP, carrying the traffic when the Interconnect does not. Tested on the same quarterly failover as the Interconnect's second attachment.

element.name: Analytics Cloud NAT
element.documentation: Regional NAT for the Dataflow workers' egress to the package mirrors and nothing else; the data never leaves by it.

element.name: Lending Cloud NAT
element.documentation: Regional NAT for the private subnetworks' egress, the only way out that is not a Private Service Connect endpoint; one gateway per region, not one per zone.

element.name: Lending Proxy-only Subnetwork
element.documentation: The proxy-only subnetwork the regional external load balancer's proxies sit in; nothing of ours runs there, and nothing of ours may.

element.name: Analytics Data Subnetwork
element.documentation: The analytics project's one subnetwork, for the Dataflow workers and the Composer environment; BigQuery and Pub/Sub are reached over Private Google Access rather than through it.

element.name: Analytics Data Subnetwork (DR)
element.documentation: The warm-standby region's subnetwork for the analytics jobs, empty until a failover. BigQuery keeps the dataset in a multi-region of its own, so what fails over is the jobs and the schedule, not the data.

element.name: APQC Process Classification Framework
element.documentation: A reference framework. A cross-industry process taxonomy. Used here for the enabling tier, where a card-specific name adds nothing: finance, HR and corporate services look much the same in any industry, and inventing local names for them costs comparability for no benefit.

element.name: BIAN
element.documentation: A reference framework. The Banking Industry Architecture Network's service landscape. A reference model of banking service domains, organized into business areas. Strong on what a bank does and deliberately silent on how it is run.

element.name: BIZBOK
element.documentation: A reference framework. The Business Architecture Guild's body of knowledge. Governs how the capability map and the value streams are built rather than what is in them, which makes it the framework this repository's own business layer answers to.

element.name: COBIT 2019
element.documentation: A reference framework. Governance and management objectives for enterprise IT. Where ITIL says how to run a service, this says how to know whether it is being run well, which is why the risk and technology governance domains answer to it.

element.name: CRI Profile
element.documentation: A reference framework. The Cyber Risk Institute's Profile: the financial sector's harmonization of NIST CSF, ISO 27001 and the regulators' expectations into one set of diagnostic statements. What a bank is examined against for cyber, and therefore what the security domain is governed by rather than informed by.

element.name: DAMA-DMBOK
element.documentation: A reference framework. The data management body of knowledge: governance, quality, architecture, metadata, master data, security. The only one of these with a defensible account of what a data function is responsible for.

element.name: ISO/IEC 27001
element.documentation: A reference framework. The certifiable information security management standard. Named separately from the NIST framework because certification is a fact about the organization and a practice framework is not.

element.name: ITIL 4
element.documentation: A reference framework. Service management practice: incident, change, problem, service level. The frame technology operations is actually run and audited against, and the vocabulary a service management tool already speaks.

element.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
element.documentation: A reference framework. Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. The five functions most security programs are structured and reported against, and the one framing a board recognizes.

element.name: PCI DSS
element.documentation: A reference framework. The card industry's data security standard. Not a framework anybody chose: it is a condition of processing card transactions, which is why it governs the payment and merchant domains whatever anyone thinks of it.

element.name: TOGAF
element.documentation: A reference framework. The architecture development method and content metamodel this repository's entity types are drawn from. It governs the practice of architecture, not any business domain, which is why nothing but the architecture function maps to it.
